paper_metadata.title: Applying QNLP to sentiment analysis in finance

summary: The paper evaluates two QNLP approaches—QLSTM and DisCoCat—for financial sentiment analysis on ~1000 ChatGPT-generated sentences. QLSTM achieves validation accuracies above 80% similar to a classical LSTM baseline but requires ~10 hours of simulation for the more complex dataset, while the DisCoCat implementation performs poorly (≈50% accuracy) and requires ~82 hours of CPU simulation for 100 epochs.

experiments.description: QLSTM sentiment-analysis experiment on synthetic finance sentences, evaluated on low- and moderate-complexity datasets and compared against a classical LSTM baseline.

algorithm.ansatz: Original QLSTM ansatz from Chen et al. (data input layer, variational layer, measurement layer)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for up to 200 epochs; performance assessed over training curves

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Current input vector xt and previous hidden state ht-1 are concatenated into vt and fed into the QLSTM cell; the paper does not specify a formal amplitude/basis encoding beyond the QLSTM data-input ansatz
problem_formulation.objective_function: sentiment classification over synthetic finance sentences

problem_instance.description: Synthetic finance sentiment analysis with ChatGPT-generated sentences labeled negative/neutral/positive; QLSTM evaluated on both low- and moderate-complexity datasets.

dataset_specification.description: Low complexity: max length 5 words; Moderate complexity: detailed sentences; labels negative=0, neutral=1, positive=2

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: ChatGPT used to generate grammatically structured finance-related sentences; labels appended in generation prompt; no further preprocessing details reported
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 80/10/10 train/validation/test split; training curves reported over epochs; compared to classical LSTM baseline

hardware.framework: PennyLane (likely) with custom QLSTM implementation; GPU-enabled simulator mentioned but backend unspecified

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: ChatGPT-based synthetic data generation; hyperparameter tuning for QLSTM and baseline LSTM
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Binary cross entropy evaluation and accuracy/loss tracking over epochs
implementation_details.total_execution_time: about 10 hours for the moderate-complexity QLSTM simulation

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: low complexity converges within about 20 epochs; moderate complexity shows delayed learning and possible barren plateaus

speedup_claims.conditions: on the generated finance sentiment datasets using the reported CPU-based circuit simulation setup
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not claim asymptotic speedup; comparison is empirical and implementation-dependent.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: not analyzed; experiments limited to small circuit simulations with 4‑qubit QNN blocks inside the QLSTM cell
limiting_factors: No demonstrated improvement over classical LSTM accuracy
Possible barren plateaus observed in moderate dataset training

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports CPU/GPU-based circuit simulation and no real QPU device.
PennyLane is explicitly mentioned in the discussion of implementation support; no specific backend device is named.
No explicit circuit depth, shot count, optimizer, or parameter count is reported for the QLSTM; only qubit count and ansatz-layer count are given.
Speedup order is not characterized asymptotically; the paper only reports empirical training-time comparisons.
Paper states QLSTM achieves results 'close to classical results', not better.
Classical LSTM baseline reaches similar validation accuracy (>80%).
No claim of quantum advantage over classical baselines.

experiments.description: DisCoCat-based QNLP sentiment-analysis experiment on the low-complexity synthetic finance dataset, reduced to binary classification due to CPU simulation cost.

algorithm.variant: DisCoCat QNLP with CCG parser and lambeq/BobCatParser
algorithm.ansatz: Single-qubit words: Euler parameterization Rx(theta3) Rz(theta2) Rx(theta1); multi-qubit words: IQP layers

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Words are embedded into quantum states via parameterized rotations; sentence meaning extracted by postselection on the sentence wire
problem_formulation.objective_function: binary sentiment classification of finance sentences
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: classical postselection on wires 1 and 3 in the |0> state to extract sentence meaning

problem_instance.description: Low-complexity synthetic finance sentiment dataset generated with ChatGPT; neutral class removed for DisCoCat to enable binary classification and reduce simulation cost.

dataset_specification.description: Low complexity sentences of maximum length five words; binary labels after dropping neutral class

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: CCG parsing via BobCatParser; neutral class removed; sentence meaning extracted by postselection
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100 training epochs; loss and accuracy curves reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: ChatGPT-based sentence generation; CCG parsing with BobCatParser; neutral class dropped
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Postselection on sentence wire; binary accuracy/loss tracking
implementation_details.total_execution_time: about 82 hours of wallclock time for 100 epochs

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: slight improvement over 100 epochs; barely better than random guessing

speedup_claims.factor: slower than QLSTM; no numeric speedup factor reported
speedup_claims.conditions: same CPU-based circuit simulator setup; 100 epochs on low-complexity data
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper explicitly avoids claiming DisCoCat is worse in general; it notes that a more efficient software implementation could improve results.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: not analyzed; CPU-based DisCoCat circuit simulation required ~82 hours for 100 epochs on a small dataset
limiting_factors: CPU-only circuit simulation extremely slow (82 hours for 100 epochs)
Binary classification simplification required due to compute limits
Heavy postselection overhead in DisCoCat circuits
No demonstrated advantage vs classical NLP models

notes: The paper reports CPU-based circuit simulation and no real QPU, so hardware.type is inferred as simulator_other.

No explicit qubit count is given for DisCoCat; the paper states the sentence wire can be represented with a single qubit after dropping the neutral class, but the full circuit qubit count is not specified, so num_qubits is left null.
No explicit circuit depth or gate counts are reported for the DisCoCat experiment.
Speedup order is not characterized asymptotically; only empirical wall-clock comparison is reported.
Section IV: DisCoCat accuracy barely exceeds random guessing.
Authors explicitly state QLSTMs are faster to train than DisCoCat in their setup.
No advantage over classical methods demonstrated.
